walkthrough: Goal: start from a picture I have (a photo, a scan, a cut-out with transparency): bring it into the artwork as a layer of its own, put it where I want it, and paint over, under and on it.

Entry: on the canvas tap Actions (the spanner in the left island). The panel's first section, Add, holds Insert image… with the note 'As a new layer' (Procreate's Actions > Add > Insert a photo); Share and Canvas (Reference) follow as before. Tap it: the panel closes and the system's picker opens, offering PNG and JPEG pictures.
Cancel: Back in the picker: nothing happens, nothing is said, the artwork is as it was.

Failure: choosing a file that is not a picture (or a damaged one, or one above 50 megapixels): the top band says 'Couldn't insert the image: only PNG and JPEG images can be used.' (or why) with OK; nothing is added.

Success: choose a picture. 'Opening the image…' may show for a moment; then the picture appears centred on the canvas on a new layer named 'Inserted image', right above the layer I was on (in its group, if it has one), and the Transform tool is on at once: the Transform arrow carries the ink ring, the frame with its corner handles and turn handle lies round the picture, and the top band's bar offers Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Rotate 45° and Reset. A picture smaller than the canvas keeps its pixel size; a larger one is fitted inside the canvas with its shape kept. A phone photo comes in upright; transparent parts of a PNG stay transparent.

Place: drag inside the frame to move it, a corner to scale it, the handle above to turn it; the bar's taps flip and turn it; undo and redo step through these moves while the tool is on. Undo right after inserting (before moving) takes the picture and its layer away again.

Done: tap Transform again, or choose a brush or any other edit: the picture stays where it shows. Inserting, the layer and the placing are one step of the drawing: one undo removes the picture and its layer, redo brings both back exactly.

After: the picture's layer behaves like painted content: a Mask on it hides parts of it, a Clipping Mask layer above paints only on it, Transform moves it again, export shows it as the screen does. Reopen after the system closed the app: the picture is where it was left.

Not here: colour profiles (S27), inserting a file or a PDF, pasting, Procreate's 'Insert a flattened copy', keeping the picture's original pixels for a later re-transform (each transform resamples the layer as it is).
